tasks.short: Count supplies received against the delivery note, record receipts and consumption, count stock on the shelves, check the reorder proposal, and send reorder needs to purchasing.

steps.what: Chemical operator counts supplies received: against the paper delivery note today; after the change by scanning each item against the purchase order on the handheld
Chemical operator checks the receipt before posting: items, lots and quantities against the count, the delivery note and any damaged goods
Chemical operator posts the checked goods receipt against the purchase order

Chemical operator records supplies received and consumed: on the paper stock list today; after the change receipts come from the posted scan and consumption from the batch records, and the operator checks the stock record

Chemical operator counts the inventory on the shelves each week: on a paper list compared with the stock list today; after the change entering each count on the handheld, which compares it with the booked stock
Chemical operator checks the reorder proposal: items and quantities against the shelf count and the coming batches
Chemical operator releases the checked reorder list to purchasing: by e-mail today, as one requisition release in the ERP after the change

tasks.design: Received supplies are scanned against the purchase order in the ERP ({ERP}) and the operator checks the receipt and posts it once, and consumption is booked from the batch records in the production system, so the paper stock list goes. The weekly shelf count uses a handheld that shows expected quantities. Reorder points in the ERP propose orders; the operator checks the list and releases it once to purchasing as a requisition. Counting stays with the operator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Receipts and use were written on paper lists and reorders e-mailed.
tasks.enabler_now: ERP goods receipt by scan and reorder points are standard.
tasks.still_hard: Partly used drums and bags are hard to count.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting a damaged drum that should not go into stock.
tasks.altitude: The operator checks proposals instead of keeping lists.

evidence.claim: ERP systems book goods receipts by scan, consumption from production records, and propose orders from reorder points.
Systems that can monitor staff performance, such as per-operator scan logs, need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the delivery to the reorder sent; ordering from suppliers is outside.
Input contract: purchase orders and batch records in the systems; fallback is paper lists.

Counting, the receipt check, the posting and the reorder check stay with the operator. s1 keeps 80 because counting stays and only matching lines to the delivery note goes; s2 keeps 20 for checking the stock record; s3 keeps 85 because each count is still entered; s5 keeps 10 for the release itself.
Purchasing works from requisitions as it did from e-mails.
research_questions: Do stock differences at the count fall?

incremental.description: Chemical operator corrects bookings when a scan is missed.

approvals.approved_version: The reorder requisition with items and quantities exactly as checked by the operator in s4, released once to purchasing as a requisition in the {ERP}; any change needs a new check.
The goods receipt with items, lots and quantities exactly as checked by the operator in s1b, posted once against the purchase order in the {ERP}; any correction needs a new check and posting.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many partly used drums and bags and goods without barcodes, so half of the stock record is still kept by hand (29.5); high: barcoded deliveries and batch records in the systems (41.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The chemical operator keeps counting and checking supplies; paper stock lists and e-mailed reorders shrink.
skills_to_grow: Scanning receipts and checking reorder proposals
role.ambitious_version: An operator with more time on the process.
